title: One of the First Webcams Ever Watched a Coffee Pot at Cambridge

scenes.text: One of the first webcams ever watched a coffee pot.
In 1991, Cambridge researchers pointed a camera at the Trojan Room coffee pot.
Their team worked on different floors, and nobody knew when a fresh pot was ready.
The picture was tiny and grainy, and it updated about three times a minute.
In 1993 it went on the web, and the whole world could watch coffee.
In 2001 it was switched off, and the coffee machine sold on eBay for over three thousand pounds.

description:
One of the first webcams ever watched a coffee pot at Cambridge.
In 1991 researchers pointed a camera at the Trojan Room coffee pot so people could see if it was full. It went on the web in 1993 and the pot later sold on eBay for 3,350 pounds.
What would you point a webcam at? Comment below.
first_comment: The picture refreshed about three times a minute. What do you think people watched on the early web instead?
